ch.s: Verses 1–10: “A copy of a letter that Jeremy sent to those who were to be led captives into Babylon by the king of the Babylonians, to give them the…”; Verses 11–20: “They will even give some of it to the common prostitutes. They dress them like men with garments, even the gods of silver, gods of gold, and gods…”; Verses 21–30: “when their faces are blackened through the smoke that comes out of the temple.”; Verses 31–40: “And in their temples the priests sit on seats, having their clothes torn and their heads and beards shaven, and nothing on their heads.”; Verses 41–50: “If they shall see one mute who can’t speak, they bring him and ask him to call upon Bel, as though he were able to understand.”; Verses 51–60: “It will be manifest to all nations and kings that they are no gods, but the works of men’s hands, and that there is no work of God…”; Verses 61–70: “Likewise also the lightning when it flashes is beautiful to see. In the same way, the wind also blows in every country.”; Verses 71–73: “Likewise also their gods of wood overlaid with gold and with silver are like a white thorn in an orchard that every bird sits upon. They are also…”. Places: Babylon.
q: Read verses 1–10. What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 11–20, what do you learn about leadership and kingship?
Read verse 73 slowly. What does it say about God, about people, and about how to live?
Where do you see the theme of salvation and redemption in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of Letter of Jeremiah?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.a: Thank God for His deliverance, and share what He has done for you with one person.
